reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer reports describe a combined biochemical and molecular-dynamics investigation of ATP-dependent regulation. Final-paper support is provided by P:S-7ea22fc8ec472dd7dd21 for the apo-enzyme activity experiments and P:S-d4b0f240e588b84988d9 for the MD entry/exit analysis.

Reviewer reports identify ATP-specific enhancement of FAD-dependent activity and an allosteric network as the central experimental and mechanistic findings. Final-paper support is provided by P:S-5513820c271ecf84f959 and P:S-20e7b1e8d5766ab8da25.

Reviewers frame the work as an investigation of ATP allosteric regulation of ACOX-1.1 and a potential ATP entry/exit mechanism. Final-paper support is provided by P:S-87f1885d625e6658766c and P:S-c29eb8d8925e0b36ac6b, which describe the ATP-dependent mechanism and the unusual ATP-binding domain.

The reviewer limited the broader significance because biological implications were insufficiently explored. The response acknowledges that the relevant C. elegans ATP concentrations are unknown, and final-paper span P:S-68e7051b8be65a5a2513 independently retains that uncertainty.

The reviewer questioned whether the inferred high- and low-affinity FAD states were independently established. The response reports confirmation of the high-affinity site but states that its assay cannot confirm the low-affinity site; final-paper spans P:S-ffea3eb68f16366486fc and P:S-b50bbb26bcaecb728f88 retain the two-population account as an interpretation or suggested model.

Reviewers asked whether the relevant cellular ATP and FAD concentrations support the proposed regulation. The response and final-paper span P:S-68e7051b8be65a5a2513 both state that ATP concentrations in C. elegans organelles and tissues are not known.

Audit-only resolved kinetic-reporting concern: the response reports added FAD and ATP affinity measurements, and final-paper support appears in P:S-acb299ee5b5bb57952f6. The subsequent reviewer report states that the comments were addressed.

Audit-only resolved MD-representative-structure concern: the response reports clustering of apo and holo trajectories and revised comparisons; P:S-acb299ee5b5bb57952f6 describes the clustering procedure. The final reviewer report states that all concerns were addressed.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Clarify the physiological settings in which this regulatory mechanism is likely to operate.
limiting_points.text: The broader biological significance remains constrained because the relevant ATP concentrations in C. elegans tissues and organelles are not established.

supporting_points.text: The work identifies ATP-dependent allosteric regulation of ACOX-1.1 through enhanced FAD affinity and examines an unusual buried ATP-binding site.

questions.suggested_action: Determine ATP and free-FAD concentrations in the relevant C. elegans cellular compartments or define conditions that test the proposed regulatory regime.
questions.text: Under which C. elegans cellular or organellar ATP and free-FAD concentrations does ATP-dependent control of ACOX-1.1 operate?

strengths.text: The study combines apo-enzyme biochemical assays with molecular-dynamics analysis to investigate ATP-dependent regulation and ligand-site accessibility.
The evidence links ATP specificity and ATP-site or allosteric-network perturbations to FAD-dependent enzymatic activity.

summary.text: The study investigates ATP-dependent allosteric regulation of C. elegans ACOX-1.1, combining biochemical measurements with molecular-dynamics analysis of FAD and ATP binding-site behavior. Reviewer reports support the specific contribution while identifying two remaining limits: the two-population FAD-binding interpretation is not fully independently resolved, and the physiological ATP and FAD regime in C. elegans remains unknown.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Distinguish the directly measured high-affinity ATP-dependent FAD interaction from the inferred low-affinity population with an independent measurement.
weaknesses.text: The proposed division into ATP-responsive high-affinity and ATP-unresponsive low-affinity enzyme populations remains an interpretation rather than a fully independently established mechanism.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The physiological framing was expanded, but the paper retains that ATP concentrations in C. elegans tissues and organelles are unknown.

The high-affinity ATP-dependent FAD interaction received additional support, but the response reports that the assay cannot confirm the low-affinity state, which remains modeled as a two-population interpretation.
Added affinity measurements and kinetic-model details address the concerns about cofactor occupancy and kinetic reporting.
Trajectory clustering and the revised representative-structure comparison address the MD-comparability and selection concern.
